passage_text: Researchers at the University of Health Sciences conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a novel antihypertensive agent, Hypertensol, compared with standard therapy in adults with stage 1 hypertension. The study enrolled 200 participants (100 per arm) and measured systolic blood pressure (SBP) at baseline and after 8 weeks of treatment. In addition, adverse events and adherence were recorded. The investigators hypothesized that Hypertensol would produce a greater mean reduction in SBP than standard therapy. The study was double‑blinded, and all participants received a matching placebo capsule to maintain blinding. Data were analyzed on an intention‑to‑treat basis. The results are summarized in Table 1 below. The authors reported that Hypertensol produced a 1.2 mm Hg greater mean reduction in SBP than standard therapy (95% CI −0.2 to 2.6).
stem: According to Table 1, which statement best describes the change in systolic blood pressure for the Hypertensol group?

options.A: The mean SBP increased by 8.7 mm Hg.
options.B: The mean SBP decreased by 8.7 mm Hg.
options.C: The mean SBP decreased by 7.5 mm Hg.

explanation: The table shows a mean change of –8.7 mm Hg for the Hypertensol group, indicating a reduction in SBP.
trap: Reading the negative change (−8.7) as a rise in pressure, when a negative change means SBP fell.

stem: Which study design best supports causal inference about the effect of Hypertensol compared with standard therapy?
explanation: Correct: Random assignment to Hypertensol or standard therapy, with blinding, balances known and unknown confounders so a difference in SBP can be attributed to the drug. Why the others are wrong: A) a cross-sectional study measures one time point and cannot show change after treatment. B) a case-control study starts from outcomes and looks back, so it cannot assign treatment. D) an observational cohort has no random assignment, so confounding can remain.
trap: Option D is tempting because cohort studies are prospective, but they still lack randomization.

stem: According to Table 1, what was the mean change in SBP from baseline for the standard therapy group?
explanation: Correct: Table 1 lists −7.5 mm Hg for the Standard Therapy group, a reduction. Why the others are wrong: B) −8.7 mm Hg is the Hypertensol change, not the standard-therapy change. C) 7.5 mm Hg has the right size but the wrong sign; pressure fell. D) 8.7 mm Hg has the Hypertensol size and the wrong sign.
trap: Reading the Hypertensol row (−8.7) instead of the Standard Therapy row, or dropping the minus sign.

stem: According to the passage, why did all participants receive a matching placebo capsule?

options.A: To keep participants and investigators unaware of which active treatment each participant received
options.B: To raise the dose of drug delivered to each participant
options.C: To create an untreated comparison group
options.D: To make baseline SBP identical in the two arms

explanation: Correct: The passage states the matching placebo capsule was used to maintain double blinding. Why the others are wrong: B) a placebo contains no drug and cannot raise the dose. C) both arms received an active drug, so no group was untreated. D) baseline balance comes from randomization, not from placebo.
trap: Assuming a placebo is always used to create an untreated group, even though both arms here received active treatment.

stem: The passage reports a 1.2 mm Hg greater mean reduction with Hypertensol than with standard therapy (95% CI −0.2 to 2.6). Which is the best interpretation?

options.A: The difference is statistically significant at the 0.05 level because the point estimate is positive.
options.B: The interval includes 0, so the data do not show a statistically significant difference at the 0.05 level.
options.C: Hypertensol is significantly worse than standard therapy.
options.D: The true difference is exactly 1.2 mm Hg.

explanation: Correct: A 95% CI that includes 0 means the difference is not statistically significant at α = 0.05. Why the others are wrong: A) significance depends on whether the interval excludes 0, not on the sign of the estimate. C) the estimate favors Hypertensol, and nothing shows it is worse. D) 1.2 is only the best estimate; the interval shows the plausible range.
trap: Treating a positive point estimate as proof of a significant benefit even though the confidence interval includes 0.
